source.title: Multi-scale Feature Learning Dynamics: Insights for Double Descent
source.authors: M. Pezeshki; Amartya Mitra; Yoshua Bengio; Guillaume Lajoie

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and figures are represented as flattened text or image placeholders.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes and experimentally measures epoch-wise generalization-error dynamics using a linear teacher-student model and a ResNet-18, a different setup from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study's CIFAR-10 experiment uses 15% training-label noise and varies weight decay over training time. Its teacher-student analysis and simulations examine epoch-wise double descent. It does not test the listed versions' natural-label memorization, width, convolutional advantage, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example claims. Values used to make figures are not separately reported numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: The study measures epoch-wise test-error dynamics at fixed architecture, varying weight decay and feature learning scales. None of V1–V8 predicts this comparison. In particular, training longer does not test V2's prediction about increasing width. References to the listed original studies provide context rather than new tests of their claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors explain epoch-wise double descent through fast features overfitting before slower features improve prediction. Their analytical predictions match teacher-student simulations, while the ResNet-18 experiment provides qualitative agreement rather than direct verification of feature learning rates in deep networks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies epoch-wise double descent using a linear teacher-student model and a CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 trained with label noise; it does not reproduce the methods in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The generalization-error trajectory changes with weight-decay strength and with the teacher-student feature condition number κ.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with 15% fixed label corruption, intermediate weight decay produces an initial test-error decrease followed by overfitting; smaller weight decay produces epoch-wise double descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay can change the shape of test-error trajectories over training time in noisy-label image classification.

fits_no_version.finding: The linear teacher-student model exhibits epoch-wise double descent when fast features overfit before slower features are learned. At κ = 100000, the reported trajectory instead exhibits conventional overfitting. Simulations closely match the analytical predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different feature learning scales can produce epoch-wise double descent, with its appearance depending on regularization and the separation of learning scales.

record.code_released: GitHub repository and Colab notebook are mentioned, but no URL is stated in the supplied text.
record.problems: The real-network experiment uses label noise rather than natural labels and reports qualitative figure-based results without numeric values in the text. The authors note that the teacher-student setup is linear and lacks the finer dynamics of nonlinear, multilayer networks.

untested.parts: No comparison of natural-label generalization with near-perfect fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy under fully random labels.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison or test of local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison under limited or broader tuning.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No dropout comparison, training-set-size interaction, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measure, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures address a different comparison; this does not deny the reported epoch-wise effects. The supplied document is marked as a preprint and does not establish the record's ICML publication claim.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare natural labels with fixed random labels or report random-label fit and held-out accuracy.
Does not sweep network width past the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD for held-out performance.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with other generalization measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples.
